text:
Brady Skjei is one of the fastest skaters in the league, 98th percentile in top speed, and Nashville leans on him for about 20 minutes a night. The Predators have won five straight, and he has an assist in four of their last eight games.

The underlying numbers are harder on him. Nashville takes 43% of the expected goals at five on five with Skjei on the ice and does better with him on the bench, and the defencemen he most resembles share big minutes, penalty kills and chances piling up against. Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level last season. He has no goals this year, and the range we'd expect from here is about four over a full season. The skating is the tool worth watching: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 41% of his entries, and carries led to a chance 25% of the time against 8% for dump-ins. If he uses that speed more, the offence follows. If he doesn't, he's a big contract doing replacement-level work.
